title: Punt TO: Player Targets
brief: Which high-usage players gain value for us if we ignore turnovers, and how should they be tiered by price? It must explain why experts ignore TO in head-to-head leagues and that streaming for games raises turnovers anyway.
summary: In our 9-cat H2H league, plan to punt turnovers from the start. Every first-round player commits a lot of them, and streaming for games adds more anyway. Target high-usage, high-assist players whose only weak category is TO, and pay expert prices, not the inflated Yahoo market.

sections.heading: Why experts ignore turnovers in H2H

paragraphs.text: Several experts ignore turnovers completely in head-to-head leagues. One says that anyone drafting high-usage, high-value players should punt TO, because those players cannot avoid them.

The reason is built into the stat. Turnovers are a third of the usage formula, so every first-round player has high turnovers. If you pay top prices in our auction, you are already losing TO most weeks. Do not spend money trying to fix it.
TO is the only negative counting stat in our format. That makes it the cheapest category to give up. You still compete for the other 8, and 5 wins out of 9 takes the week.

In H2H you want to max out games played. Our league has daily lineups and up to 6 acquisitions per week, so streaming for extra games is a core weekly tactic. Every extra game adds turnovers. Chasing low turnovers works against the way you win H2H weeks.

The reverse also holds. Injuries and short schedules cut your turnovers on their own. In weeks when you have fewer games than your opponent, you often win TO without trying. A punt TO team will still steal the category some weeks.

For the same reason, one ranking expert pushes centers down in H2H. Traditional box score values overrate blocks, steals and some percentages, and they reward low turnovers that matter less when you stream for games.

sections.heading: What punting TO pulls you toward

paragraphs.text: Categories move together. High assists go with high turnovers. Low turnovers go with low points and assists. So a punt TO team should lean into assists and points from high-usage guards and playmaking forwards, because those are the players other builds avoid.

High blocks go with high rebounds and FG%. Pair your high-usage creators with a big who supplies those three. Wembanyama is a natural anchor here, but his profile note says you still need a second shot blocker. Jaren Jackson Jr. and Zach Edey are cheaper ways to add blocks and rebounds.

Punt TO combines well with a second punt. Giannis anchors a punt FT% build. Trae Young, LaMelo Ball and James Harden fit punt FG% builds. Sengun and Castle fit punt FT% builds. Check that your second punt does not cut into the assists and points you are building around.

The experts differ in degree. One side ignores turnovers completely in every head-to-head league. The other says low turnovers simply matter less in H2H, and the same expert who ignores TO also says it is fine to use turnovers as a tiebreaker between two otherwise identical players. In practice, never pay extra for low turnovers, but if two players are level on your board, take the one with fewer.

sections.heading: Tiering by price at our auction

paragraphs.text: Anchors are the top players whose only clear weakness is turnovers: Jokić, Wembanyama, Dončić, Giannis and Tatum. For a punt TO team they lose nothing. Their auction prices still run above formula value, so set your max bid before the draft on October 18.

Fit alone does not justify the market price. Edwards, Cunningham, Mitchell, Jalen Johnson, Flagg, Barnes, Giddey and Trae Young all fit punt TO. But the experts value each of them well below the Yahoo market. Bid up to the expert cap and then let others pay. Edwards, Ball, Mitchell and Harden also have two-game weeks in our playoffs.

The best value comes in the middle and late rounds. Jaren Jackson Jr., Keyonte George, Garland, Dejounte Murray and Edey cost well below their expert value. Murray's only flagged weakness is turnovers, and he adds clear steals and assists. Late in the draft, use bench spots on flyers like Queen and Jalen Green. Use an IL slot to stash Ingram while he recovers.

In the first weeks, check assists and minutes for every punt TO target. Assists are what you are paying for. For Cunningham, Giddey, Ball, Reaves and Castle, that is the number that shows whether the build is working. If a high-turnover player loses his assists, he no longer fits, so trade him before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
